_about: Legal's banned rows for the moveset generator (docs/legal/movegen-screen.md). For Combat to merge into parts.json as `strike.banned` and `strike.bannedSequences`. A row matches when every field it names matches; a field with a list matches if any value in it matches. Fields are the grammar's own: limb, tip, path, target, weight, form, arms, plus `flags` for a property of how a piece is posed. The rows describe shapes, not sources. The generator must refuse to emit a piece, or a string, that matches a row, and the build must fail if one slips through.

banned.why: two hands with wrists together pushed forward: a famous beam-release pose
hands cupped at a hip, or drawn back to one hip and thrust: the franchise's best-known wind-up. Applies to every weight and every form, including held heavies
banned.appliesTo: open or clawed hands (a closed fist chambered at the hip is a punch chamber and passes b02; h05 still holds a 12-tick wind-up to the shoulder)

banned.why: a rising blow with a leap or a spin, by hand, elbow or knee: the jumping, turning uppercut
banned.appliesTo: any tip of a hand, elbow or knee on a rise path to the jaw or head: a rising blow bound by this row whatever its tip (Combat's strict reading)

banned.why: more than a single turn, or a spin that travels: a multi-hit whirling kick
two clasped fists brought down: the double axe-handle smash
a clawed hand or grip on the face
grips on the throat, hair or tail are never used (the grab rules)
an arm passing through the body
a melee piece never carries light, a ball or a raised charging pose
two fingers or a pointing finger, or a hand to the forehead: the franchise's beam and teleport poses
a held or charged medium or heavy is loaded with one arm drawn back at shoulder height, never at a hip and never with both hands together; the new words medium and charged loosen nothing
no vanish or blink between blows; the fighter is drawn the whole way

banned.rule: a leap is allowed for a knee or a foot to the gut, chest or legs (the Hopper's hop; the cleared drop kick); never with a hand, elbow or the head as the striking limb, and never to the jaw or head by any limb (b03); one body height at most, the landing drawn, no hover or held flight pose, a single turn at most (b04)
banned.why: the jumping rising uppercut and its kin; ruled 2026-10-12 for the Hopper

bannedSequences.rule: no more than 3 pieces in a row with the same limb, tip and path
bannedSequences.why: a barrage of identical blows is a famous shouted-barrage signature

bannedSequences.rule: no more than 2 blows in a row to the same target, and never two to the gut in a row
bannedSequences.why: a stomach-punch trade; also keeps Blow for Blow ours

bannedSequences.rule: a flurry never repeats a shouted syllable across its blows
bannedSequences.why: a chanted barrage; audio and the generator both enforce it

bannedSequences.rule: a spin is never followed by another spin, and never by a head kick
bannedSequences.why: a multi-turn whirl; also the grammar's light rule

bannedSequences.rule: a rising blow is never followed by another rising blow while he is airborne
a launch is never followed by a clasped two-hand overhead blow
no string places a piece after a step that is not drawn: no vanish, blink or teleport step

inside a hold, vicious blows run no more than 2 in a row to the same place, and the arm counts as three places (shoulder, elbow, wrist) and the head, core and legs as two each, so four taps on one region alternate places; vicious blows are strikes, never a grip on the throat, hair or tail, and never a clawed hand on the face; the sound rule f03 holds across the taps
bannedSequences.why: s02 applied to the clinch; Orb's design and the rating question are still open (not cleared by this row)

bannedSequences.rule: a sole or heel brought down from above: on a standing opponent, any target above the knee is allowed (the cleared stomp and axe kick); on a downed opponent, the torso and limbs only; the head, face, neck and groin of a downed opponent are out of the base moveset until the rating decision (a finisher only, not repeatable, never in a public trailer, run through the questionnaires first)
bannedSequences.why: ratings (PEGI 18 treats violence towards defenceless people as its own descriptor; stricter markets) rather than IP; the Hopper's stomp, ruled 2026-10-12

motion.rule: a zip (any reading) is drawn on every tick: the body is visible and opaque on each tick of the way in and the way out, never hidden, faded or swapped for a copy
a zip's way in and its way out each last at least 4 ticks, and consecutive drawn positions are at most 3 body heights apart (ticks >= max(4, ceil(distance in bh / 3)))
motion.why: a zero or two-tick jump with echoes is a blink step

motion.rule: the path is continuous: the body passes through every point between start and arrival, and any copy or echo trails behind the body, never ahead of it, never at the arrival point before the body gets there
motion.why: an afterimage that stands where he is about to appear is the vanish-step staging

motion.rule: a far-side exit is its own drawn travel that starts after the strike hold, over the rival or round him, with the rival's body in view throughout; he never appears behind the rival in the same tick as the strike
motion.why: the appear-behind-you beat needs the vanish

motion.rule: a zip ghost is a flat single tint in the fighter's lane colour (never the body's own colours or face), opacity 0.35 or less and fainter for older ones, at most 5 per zip, on the body's real recent path, each overlapping the next by about a third so they read as a smear, never in a ring, fan or spread round the target, gone within 8 ticks of the zip's end
motion.why: filled ghosts are allowed as a blur, not as a lineup of body copies

motion.rule: the body is always drawn on top of its ghosts at full opacity, and no ghost stays behind as a stationary copy
motion.why: a decoy copy is a separate signature

motion.rule: a heavy's wind-up ring is hollow, thin, in the lane colour, shrinks onto the striking fist and never grows or holds, lasts the wind-up only (10 ticks or fewer), and never fills or becomes a ball at the hand
motion.why: a charging-pose cue under the stacking rule

motion.rule: outcome marks (counter bar, closing ring, brackets, guard fragments) carry no text or numbers, never sit on the eyes or face, and are never a full-screen or body-wide gold, white or red flash
motion.why: no readout or scanner look, no mark 7

motion.rule: in a zip chain each hop meets m01 to m08 on its own: the strike pose is held at least 4 ticks at contact with the body drawn, the ghosts on screen across the whole chain are at most 5, no ghost is left behind or placed round the target, and there is no camera cut or flash between hops
a zip at a launched rival follows his drawn body along a continuous path; it never snaps to where he will land
a slip or a step that goes behind the rival is drawn travel of at least 4 ticks with the rival in view (m04)

body ghosts (whole-figure copies from any source: zip, press styles, tech echoes, Animation's after-images) are budgeted per fighter at any instant: at most 5 round one fighter from all sources together, so at most 10 on screen with two fighters; limb ghosts stay under f01 (2 of one limb, 4 in all per fighter). Every ghost keeps m05: a flat lane tint, 0.35 opacity or less, on the fighter's own recent path, overlapping along it as a smear, never placed round the target or in a ring, gone within 8 ticks, the body on top. The 5 is a bright line for the build's gate, not a legal cliff, and may be revised on evidence (stills and the per-tick breakdown) from VFX and Rendering
motion.why: m05 and m09 made explicit per fighter and across sources

energy.rule: no sphere or ball in or at the hand, at rest or growing; a charge is light on the forearm plate or hand edge, and the blast leaves along a line
an energy hand is open or a blade, no higher than the shoulder; never cupped, never both hands pushed from the chest or drawn to a hip, never wrists together (b01, b02)
no two extended fingers, no single pointing finger as an emitter; the pinch is thumb to forefinger only (b10)
energy.why: the beam and the death-beam poses

energy.rule: a short beam or charged shot is a plain straight line: no spiral, drilling or twisting beam; a second hand may brace the arm but never grips the firing wrist and never sits cupped under it

a volley is one motion of one hand or arm (a sweep, a flick or a single thrust) that releases the fan; never both palms pumping forward in turn or one hand pumping repeatedly, and no repeated shouted syllable across it (s03)

a burst, a blast and a ki-style flurry (B), and an energy blow in reach (RB + X or Y), are thrown by one hand at shoulder height or lower: an open hand, a blade hand, or the rival's lit fist with the light on its plate and knuckle edges only (the cleared fist glow), never a ball or glow round the fist; a flurry varies the piece (hand state, release, body) and never pumps the same hand repeatedly or both palms in turn; a point-blank blast shows its flash as a thin edge or short cone at the hand, never a ball; never aimed at the face. The repeat rule counts the hand, the release and the delivery (a bolt, or a blast braced on a held pose for 12 ticks that lands once and ends the brawl): a blast after a bolt of the same hand and release is not a repeat, because the blast is its own piece and cannot be a pump. Two bolts of the same hand, release and delivery in a row stay refused (e09)
energy.why: the shouted two-palm barrage and the held sphere; the lit fist was cleared in RL-062 and is not banned by e02 or e06; clarified 2026-10-12 for Combat (the delivery counts)

energy.rule: a beam held and steered by the player stays a plain straight line; steering moves the aim or the origin only, never twists, spirals or whips the beam, and the firing pose does not change while it is held

R1 adopted: an energy blow in reach is one open, blade or lit-fist hand at shoulder height or lower, lit as a thin edge before it lands, the shot going off at contact as a thin edge or short cone, each body taking a rim of its colour on the near side and never a flash over the whole body; never at the face; mashed, the piece changes every blow (hand state, release) and at most one blow in 20 ticks gets the full flash; the blast's 12-tick wind-up is a held pose (h05) with its gather a thin ring or edge at the palm; the blade hand is a flat blade, never a pointed finger or two fingers (e03)
energy.why: R1 with the lit fist and the finger rule added

energy.rule: a mashed run of point-blank bolts must read as varied on screen, not only in data: no two bolts in a row with the same arm, path and place; no regular left-right alternation (an irregular order, with the free arm taking a bolt now and then); at least three different paths (line, outward arc, inward arc) in any five; each hand lands below the collar line on the chest or gut and never at the neck, throat or face; the two bodies keep a hand's width between the heads
energy.why: e06 for a mashed run: the same arm pumping, or two palms pumping in turn, is the barrage image

energy.rule: a beam cast pose (the signature beam and any other): one arm out, the palm or its heel leading, is allowed when the other hand never grips, braces or cups the firing wrist or forearm and stays at least shoulder width from it (open, in guard, or low at the rear); never both palms; no ball, sphere or glow held in either hand; no scream; the charge pose keeps h05 (one arm drawn back at shoulder height or lower, never at a hip); the beam is a plain straight line (e04, e07)
energy.why: RL-038's condition was the wrist-gripped palm-forward brace; the palm-forward one-arm release without that brace is an ordinary energy-in-reach hand. Closed 2026-10-16

grabs.rule: a hold point is the collar, shoulder, upper arm, body, waist or ankle; never the throat, the hair or a tail (b07), never a clawed hand on the face (b06)
no hands locked or laced between the two fighters at any time, and nothing glowing at the hands in a hold
a lift or carry is drawn whole: the carried fighter's body is in view and never hidden by a zip or a cut; a throw is a launch (the planner), not a vanish

a tackle takes the body at the waist or shoulders; the carry is drawn travel (m01 to m04 apply: at least 4 ticks, the carried body in view every tick, 3 bh a tick at most); the arrival crater is local, with debris falling and no rising ring of rubble, no lightning and no aura; a buried rival is shown partly in the ground, never hidden

a clinch is a collar-and-elbow or waist hold; the trip and the throw never lift by the throat, hair or a tail, and the two fighters' hands are never locked or laced together; no sparks or glow at the hands in the clinch
grabs.why: g01 and g02 applied to the clinch

grabs.rule: the tied pose (the clinch hold): collar-and-elbow or waist (g05); the holder's hands never lock or lace with the held fighter's; the held fighter's hands stay free and are never drawn limp, bound or pinned behind the back; both fighters upright, heads and torsos at least a forearm's length apart (a fight hold, not an embrace)

the pin is vertical against a surface (wall, building, cliff) at the shoulder, collar or upper arm; no forearm or hand across the throat or face, no choke (g01); no ground pin, mount or straddle of a downed fighter (s09's defenceless case); hips apart; the pinned fighter bears weight on his feet and is drawn struggling or bracing
grabs.why: the held fighter always has a way out; avoids the defenceless-victim reading

grabs.rule: the carry: over the shoulder or by the collar and waist; never by the head, neck, hair or tail; the carried body is drawn whole and in view every tick (g03, g04), face and chest never hidden or pressed to the holder; no sparks or glow at the hands (g02); the throw at its end is a launch through the planner, never a vanish. The tied, pinned and carried poses are class hold (h04) and the lint runs on every tick of up to 90

held.rule: held 12 ticks or more, scoped by class (see heldScope): the pair test applies to every held pose; the emitter test applies to the charge, tell, signature, energy and hold classes only

no held crossed forearms; no held arms-wide invitation. Arms wide means both arms near straight (elbows within 25 degrees of straight) and both hands 32 or more out to opposite sides, held 12 ticks or more; a shrug (elbows bent 40 degrees or more, palms up, shoulders raised) is not arms wide. A taker's open-armed stance belongs to the rival's On the Chin alone
held.why: the power pose and the take-it stance

held.rule: a signature's tell is its own stance, never a crouch with fists clenched at the sides, and carries no scream

held-lint classes for the new holds: a held X, Y or B charge pose and the tackle's coil are class charge; the seize, breaker, lift and slip tells are class tell; the clinch hold is class hold; the 45-tick taunt is class gesture; an open-hand chamber in a charged melee blow keeps the wrist at x 9 or more (not drawn to the hip), a closed-fist chamber at the hip is allowed
held.why: so the lint reaches the new poses

held.rule: a medium or heavy wind-up of 12 ticks or more is a held pose of class charge and is judged at every tick by h01 to h04: the loaded limb at shoulder height or lower (a leg may be chambered), never at a hip for any hand state, never both hands together, no limb held above 80 except in the last 6 ticks before contact, no held crossed forearms, no light and no aura; both-hand blows (a double palm or hammer) keep the hands at least shoulder width apart; a stand-in played on a longer wind-up than it was posed for is judged on the longer one (W1)
held.why: W1 adopted; a long visible wind-up is a held pose

held.rule: a deep sink (the heaving drive) is a lunge-low stance with the striking limb loaded and the other hand up in guard; never both fists clenched at the sides in a crouch, and never with a scream, an aura or ground cracking; the falling drive's rise is the body straightening or stepping up, never a leap (the drop kick excepted, as cleared), and the limb stays at shoulder height until he starts down
held.why: mark 1 over a held sink; the leap and the held raise

held.rule: a manner (the rival's show-off, the Protagonist's pointed) is a way of throwing, not a gesture: the rival's open tell keeps the limb drawn back (never arms spread as an invitation, never a beckon), and his limb left out after landing lasts 12 ticks or fewer; no taunt pose is part of a blow

a heave (the deep-sink rising blow) may take one sliding half step of up to about 22 units when the closing slack needs it: the rear foot stays on the ground, no leap, no rise before the blow (the stand is the heave's own), the other foot never leaves the ground; reach beyond that is a stepping drive's job, so Encounter limits a heave's slack to what the step covers
held.why: D4 and L1: grounded, never the jumping rising uppercut; a small slide is not a leap

held.rule: folded arms are a held crossed-forearms pose and fail h02 at 12 ticks or more: allowed on a sheet and as a moment under 12 ticks, never as an idle, stand-off or intro pose; a one-arm fold (a single forearm across the body, the other hand free or at the chin) is allowed
held.why: the Anti-hero's hybrid A 'arms folded high', RL-151

held.rule: a finisher's closing pose is a held gesture after a blow and must not mock a beaten rival: an offered hand is one hand, fingers together and still (no curling, no wiggle), palm sideways or toward the fallen rival and not at the camera, held low (forearm out, never drawn to a hip), never both arms, no smirk or taunt line; a raised hand (a pledge) stays at shoulder height or lower, palm out, fingers together, one hand, no light, glow, ring or ball in or above it, never overhead (the raised charging pose; any hand above 82 fails the signature and tell emitter test)
held.why: Art's Open Palm and Both Roads finisher styles, RL-159

stacking.rule: at any tick, no more than two of the seven marks (crouch with clenched fists, scream, upward flame aura, rubble ring with ground crack and wind, lightning on the body, hair change, a flash with a shouted form name); a held tell or a 45-tick charge is checked at every tick, not once
a stance tell's aura is a thin outline or short scattered streaks in the lane colour; a manoeuvre trail is thin and in the lane colour; a defensive rim of light sits on the guarding side only

a charge flash or ring (a tier mark at 16 or 24 ticks for a medium, 32 or 44 for a heavy, a full-charge flash, or the wind-up ring) is a thin ring or edge flash on the charging hand, forearm or plate, in the lane colour, 4 ticks or fewer, never body-wide, never gold, white or red, never with a shouted name; a wind-up ring is hollow, thin, lane-coloured and shrinks onto the limb (m07); a held charge shows at most two of the seven marks at any tick, and no scream at any tier. Tick counts are the design's and may change: the conditions, not the numbers, are the rule
stacking.why: marks 3, 7 and 2 across a held charge; restated to the three-strength spec

stacking.rule: a mutual throw-back, a spark-lock between two heavy commitments, a power-attack tell and a taunt's finish show no rubble ring with cracks and wind, no lightning on bodies, no body-wide aura and no gold, white or red flash; sparks sit at the contact point only

full flashes are counted over the whole screen, every effect and both fighters together: at most three in any one second, each small (a thin edge or short cone), none red, and a reduced-motion setting halves the rate; the cap is checked by a flash analysis of a recorded mashed sequence on the real build; a shared flash registry counts every full flash from every effect (energy, explosions, signatures, transformations, hit rings, beam clashes) against the cap, which is a condition before the first public release of the web build; the evidence needed is in photosensitivity-note.md
stacking.why: photosensitivity; Combat's one in 20 ticks is the same 3 a second

stacking.rule: a persistent HUD cue (a battered or low-state stroke, a pulse, a ring) changes no faster than 3 times a second and by preference 2 or fewer, is static under reduced motion and Reduce flashing, and counts in the flash check's frame like any other effect (the HUD is part of the screen); below the area threshold it is not a standard flash, but a flicker that runs for a whole match in a fixed place is held to the rate anyway
stacking.why: UI's crown at 4 Hz in thin arcs under 8,000 px

heldScope._about: Legal's scope for the held-pose lint (2026-10-06). A pose's class comes from its sequence family, or from a `_legal.class` mark on the pose or sequence. Unmarked poses in the charging, tell, signature, energy and held-heavy families are lint class charge, tell, signature, energy or hold; every other unmarked pose is rest or gesture.

energy: emitter holds, beams, channel, release, rain, finish holds

pairTest.fails: both hands within 10 units of each other AND both in the hip zone (x 14 or less, height 24 to 44); or both wrists forward and within 7 units of each other (wrists_together)
pairTest.exempt: a named gesture where one hand holds or brushes the other hand or wrist (the cuff, the dusting, the close taunt tap) with the body upright and no thrust or light after it

emitterTest.applies: classes charge, tell, signature, energy, hold
emitterTest.fails: the hand that emits or strikes next is an open or clawed hand in the hip zone with its wrist at x 8 or less (drawn to a hip then thrust); or any hand above 82 (80 plus a 2-unit tolerance for float error). A closed fist chambered at the hip (a punch chamber) and a relaxed free hand hanging at the side while the other arm acts both pass

armsWideTest.applies: class charge, tell, signature, energy, hold, and any held pose that is not marked gesture with bent elbows
armsWideTest.fails: both arms near straight and out wide, held 12 ticks or more, except the rival's On the Chin

flurry.rule: a flurry's or burst's blur follows each striking limb's real path: at any instant at most 2 ghosts of any limb and at most 4 limb-ghosts on screen in all; never extra arms, legs or fists drawn at once, never a fan of limbs round the target. This replaces the 'two ghosts per blow' wording, which does not hold at 15 blows a second. The numbers are ceilings on what is alive at one instant, not counts that must be drawn: fewer is always fine, reduced motion draws fewer, and a tech blow's 3 wire echoes that pop off in turn with never more than 2 alive at once meet it. Body ghosts of a zip fall under m05 (at most 5)
flurry.why: the many-armed barrage blur, by instant rather than by blow

flurry.rule: targets and pieces rotate across the whole string, whatever mix of X, Y and B made it: s01 and s02 count the string, not the button (no more than 2 blows in a row to the same target, never two gut blows running, no more than 3 of the same limb, tip and path)
flurry.why: a mixed flurry must not slip past the repeat rules by changing button

flurry.rule: vocal sounds in a flurry: no repeated shouted syllable across it, no shouted word, and at most one grunt for every two blows, varied
flurry.why: the chanted barrage (s03) at up to 10 blows a second

flurry.rule: a gap of under 6 ticks between blows never runs for more than 3 blows in a row, and only inside the opening of a burst; blows then slow (a held X's 4, 4, 5, 6, 8, 11, 15 gaps are within this)
flurry.why: the fastest barrage rate is allowed only as a short opening, not a sustained storm

flurry.rule: a burst (held X, eight lights) never repeats the last blow's limb, tip, path or place; no more than 2 blows in a row on one path; no piece twice in one burst; the hands alternate; the sound is one breath for the eight, never a syllable for each; no slow-motion close-up or camera cut on the burst

world.rule: a landmark has no clock face, no red and white striping, no stripes or beams of light, no antenna mast on a stepped tower, no multicolour night lighting on a tower top, and no pair of thin pale spires on a dark tower that reads as horns
world.why: originality: no real landmark's likeness and none of the earlier look-alike conditions (clock face, red and white striping, stripes or beams of light); the horns reading is a recommendation, not a condition. Kept on its own grounds; not from the withdrawn sensitivity rule

world.rule: the sun and moon discs are flat, never pure white, with no glow, bloom or flash; clouds and mountains pass in front of them only with soft edges at the sky's slew rate; the discs are in the flash set (a fast pan across a tall skyline and a town with the sun in frame, both modes), because a disc of about 15,000 px is most of the area threshold on its own

facade contrast is budgeted between adjacent elements as well as against the wall: any two neighbouring tones on a facade (glass against fin, spandrel against glass, cornice against shaft) differ by at most 0.085 of relative luminance, so a bright glass beside a fin on the sun side must not differ from it by 0.14; asserted on the data and read in the street flyby clips
world.why: striped tower faces under camera shake were a flash class; spatial stripes of 0.14 alternating at a pixel exceed the 10% step

world.rule: place names: the eleven generated names that are real towns over 15,000 people (bellhaven, larkfield, longfield, stonebridge, stonegate, sunrise, wakefield, whitefield, whiteford, whitehaven, whiterock) go on blocklist_start; any name added later is run against a real-town list before it ships; no destroyed place is named after a recognisable real city (c07)
world.why: no real city in the catastrophe, RL-149

withdrawn.why: rested on the withdrawn 'sensitivity' rule (no falling-tower imagery or wording); structural believability of open floors is Orb's design requirement, not a Legal condition
rested on the withdrawn rule; destruction may be shown and described in public. The casualty-count point is replaced by the ratings and platform notes (p01, p02)

public.rule: pages hosted on GitHub (the repository and GitHub Pages) follow GitHub's Acceptable Use Policies: no content that gratuitously depicts or glorifies violence, and a page's primary focus is not advertising or promotion; keep the graphic material and the sales copy on the store pages and the video platforms, not on the GitHub-hosted site
public.why: GitHub's rules (read 2026-10-12); independent of the rating

public.rule: a store listing's content descriptors, age gate and the questionnaire answers match the real build (graphic violence, the Cyborg's consumption, civilian casualties); public trailers and screenshots on each platform use that platform's mature-content marking and age restriction
public.why: ratings and platform rules; the Mature target frees the content, not the labelling

signature.rule: the barrage signature: three volleys, each one motion of one hand and each different (a sweep fanning five shards, a thrust sending three in a line, a flick sending one shot that splits), thrown from an upright, unhurried walk with the hands open and low between volleys; never both palms in turn, never one hand pumping, no shouted syllable repeated across the three (e05, e06, f03); the hand lit as a thin edge, never a ball; no aura, no crouch, no charge pose in the walk (k01, k02, h01); the close by hand is a heavy from his cleared pool; the three volleys carry at most one full flash (the last) and two lesser ones in any second, counted over the whole screen (k05, the margin rule); a rim on the rival on a landing, no whole-screen flash
signature.why: built from cleared parts; screened as a whole 2026-10-12

effects.rule: the shine on a striking hand (timing cue): two thin edge lines and a small hollow ring in his colour lightened, steady (no pulse or flicker), never a ball or glow, never white, on one hand at a time (k01), gone when the window closes; it is a rendering cue and not a property of the strike piece, so b09 is not engaged

the cash-in: a thin committed line and four closing corner brackets (no numbers or text, not on the face), then a double ring, a crossed crack, one thin vertical cut and two puffs of dust, 10 ticks or fewer, in lane colours

preview of Orb's thick glowing rippling beams and fiery explosions (to be screened drawn): a beam stays a plain straight line (e04, e07); its ripple is a slow, low-contrast shimmer (2 Hz or slower, under 10% luminance step) in the lane colour and never a strobing core; its start and end flashes go through the flash registry; a beam may not spiral, drill or twist; an explosion's fire is never a saturated-red flash (the red test: R/(R+G+B) of 0.8 or more with a chromaticity change over 0.2), grows over several ticks rather than a single-frame flash, is never a white or gold full-screen flash with a shouted name, and is not combined with a rubble ring, cracks and lightning on bodies (k01); both go into the required flash set before they ship
effects.why: area, red flash and stacking risks of large glowing effects

effects.rule: moving marks that repeat while a state lasts, listed with their rates and held to k06: the recharging ring steps once a second (1 Hz); the beam struggle's thin rings and lines and UI's tug ring pulse on a 20-tick beat (3 Hz, at the limit): they stay steady or at 1.5 Hz or slower under Reduce flashing (the shipped default) and Reduced motion, are strokes only with no brightness change, and are in the HUD and effects rate lists that hud_check and the flash set read

the calm beam (every beam under Reduce flashing, the default): the full beam at 0.86 strength with a 0.3 s rise, never a thin line and never a white core, is accepted only if the release set reads it at or under the primary limit in both modes; the explosion flame is read for red by the standard's own test on linear values (R/(R+G+B) of 0.8 or more with a chromaticity change over 0.2), where a cel orange can sit near 0.8 even though its gamma-encoded ratio is 0.56: the analyser, not the colour code, is the authority and must read red flashes 0 on the set with the explosions in

catastrophe.rule: photosensitivity: every catastrophe effect (a beam through the crust, magma and its glow, a mushroom cloud, an exosphere bombardment, the darkening sky) is added to the required flash set as its own worst-case clips in both modes before it ships, on the commit that carries it, under the combined rule and the margin; a planet-scale image is far larger than the 21,824 px threshold, so any luminance event on it counts as a flash at full area
catastrophe.why: the brightest and largest images in the game

catastrophe.rule: a catastrophe light event is at most one flash (one rise and one fall) per two seconds anywhere on the screen, over any effect together (the flash registry counts it), rises over at least 0.3 s and falls over at least 1 s, and has a calm form under Reduce flashing (lower peak, slower rise, no repeats) measured in the set; the darker the sky, the larger the absolute step of any glow or explosion, so a catastrophe in a darkened sky is measured in the darkened sky
catastrophe.why: a dark baseline makes the same event a bigger step

catastrophe.rule: red and magma: no saturated-red flash (R/(R+G+B) of 0.8 or more on linear values with a chromaticity change over 0.2) at any rate; magma is amber-orange with slow change; bubbling or pulsing in magma is low contrast (under a 10% step), 2 Hz or slower, irregular and unsynchronised, never a regular spot or stripe pattern over a large area; read red flashes 0 by the analyser
catastrophe.why: red-flash and pattern tests on the largest fire image

catastrophe.rule: a bombardment from the exosphere: explosions on the surface are small in screen area or fired no faster than two a second within any one screen window, never synchronised, their glow slow; the fighters' exosphere glow is a steady edge, not a pulse

a darkening sky changes under the sky's own slew limit (no band faster than 0.05 relative luminance a second, the mean 0.02) over minutes; fighters keep Art's lane-colour contrast (24 or more at the extremes) in the darkest sky; no lightning, no pulse, no reaction to a single hit

originality: avoid the genre's best-known planet-destruction images: the planet cracking along glowing fissures into a fireball (the famous anime planet blast), a ring-shaped shockwave leaving a planet or station (the Death Star), a single superlaser through a planet, a perfect hemisphere of light consuming a city (Akira), a beam piercing the planet and exiting the far side, and a villain charging a giant sphere with raised arms over his head; no ball charged above a head or in a hand; the boss's variants of abilities are our own abilities at world scale, not another fighter's named attack

the mushroom cloud: a stem-and-cap cloud is the natural shape of a very large blast and may be drawn, but it carries real-world associations: no radiation trefoil, no words 'nuclear', 'atomic', 'A-bomb' or 'H-bomb', no real city, date or event, no countdown or siren sound that evokes a real alert; in copy call it a blast cloud; it is a rating and sensitivity note, not a ban

civilian deaths across a run: casualties are shown as a count and an environmental result, not as depicted bodies or close-ups; no score, bonus, achievement, trophy or unlock for civilian deaths and no celebratory sound or flourish when the count rises; the menace meter is a power meter, not a score; no schools, hospitals or places of worship as staged targets; children are not shown as victims of graphic violence
catastrophe.why: classification boards treat rewarded violence against defenceless people as aggravating; platform achievements are public

catastrophe.rule: store and rating: the Mature target is the working assumption; the content survey and IARC are answered from the real build and the run mode (mass destruction, civilian casualties tracked, graphic violence, the Cyborg's consumption); the store descriptors and age gate match; trailers and screenshots use each platform's mature marking; console programmes (behind NDA) may be stricter on mass-casualty and real-world-referencing imagery; GitHub-hosted pages keep graphic imagery off (p01)

the line lint's sensitive words, whole-word, in two tiers. Block: A-bomb, H-bomb, mushroom cloud, fallout, nuclear, atomic, radiation, and the names of real events and places of mass harm (for example Hiroshima, Nagasaki, Chernobyl, Fukushima, 9/11, ground zero), holocaust, genocide. Review by a human: siren, countdown, bomb, school, hospital, church, mosque, synagogue, chapel, cathedral, temple, kindergarten, nursery, orphanage, meltdown, glass (as a verb for a bombed ground), and child, children or kid near a casualty word (died, dead, gone, lost, killed, victims). The same list guards place names and every generated line

lines.rule: provenance record for lines and text from any AI tool other than Claude: tool, model as named, date, brief file, what came back, and the human part (marks, choices, edits); mixed sources in one list; the public AI statement names categories (text and dialogue, code, music, graphics), never claims a line as human-written unless the record shows it, never 'human-made'; no private notes, unreleased art descriptions or NDA material goes into a consumer AI app
lines.why: Orb's disclosure rule; Gemini rewrites of homework 11, RL-153

lines.rule: a line that threatens the arena or a street (the Empress's block line, any area threat) fires only on its own trigger and never as a reaction to civilian casualties; no line makes a rising toll sound worth having (c08); insults go at an individual fighter, never a slur or an insult aimed at a real group, disability or body

the Cyborg's consumption: his hunger is aimed at fighters and wreckage, never civilians or children; no on-screen biting, chewing or swallowing of a living fighter, no eaten limbs, no chewing or swallowing sound and no gore from feeding until the rating decision (a clamp, a throw and feeding on wreckage are allowed); a depicted eating finisher takes the stomp treatment (rare, optional, never in public trailers or pages, distant, injury not depicted, no reward, questionnaires first); he never absorbs a defeated fighter to gain their power or form, never turns anyone into food or sweets, and has no belly-as-mouth gag or pink plump silhouette; 'Demon Cyborg' stays off public text
lines.why: RL-155: the nearest echoes are the genre's glutton and absorbing villains

lines.rule: boons, keepsakes, temptations and any hidden-outcome reward are never sold or unlocked with real money, and nothing paid gives a random or hidden reward, without asking Legal first (paid random rewards are treated as gambling-like by several stores and countries); a keepsake is an object and never a body part, ash or remains; no keepsake or title is earned by a death or a toll; the saved may speak, the lost are only a count
